q1_issues.issue: 'a romance' is a comma appositive on a past host clause ('opened'), so its typing atom must take the host's wrapper — (Past (Member from_justin_to_kelly romance)) — not the bare atom.

The measure scale 'gross' is invented: the text says only 'with $2.9-million' and states no dimension word, but the scale slot must be the surface dimension (stated adjective, else the stated dimension noun).
'American Idol winner' loses the proper noun 'American Idol' completely — no symbol and no Name atom — leaving Kelly Clarkson typed only as 'winner'.

q2_gaps: a proper-noun modifier inside a noun-noun compound ('American Idol winner', 'American Idol runnerup') — Compound concepts covers common-noun and adjective modifiers, and Names and casing bars joining the name to the adjacent lowercase head noun, so the show name has nowhere to go
a chart / box-office rank PP on an event ('opened at No. 11') — Ordinal is defined for an entity's rank in an NP ('the third climber'), not for a rank-position adjunct
a bare money amount as an accompaniment ('with $2.9-million') — no dimension word is stated, so Measure has no licensed scale to record
a title noun premodifying a name ('winner Kelly Clarkson') under a past host clause — unclear whether the appositive tense-wrapper rule reaches it
notes: The multi-word title as one opaque symbol + Name, the 'starring' participial post-modifier as a reduced-relative event, distributing the coordinated object into two star events, and open -> Patient (matching the instruction set's own 'the festival opened' example) are all correct. The same appositive-wrapper question arises for kc_kind and jg_kind, which sit inside the untensed participial.
